title: The Uncharted Trail
premise: Desert ranger Silas Vasquez is sent upriver to find the missing Hollis expedition, only to discover its survivors guarding a secret: a pre-war ledger proving the region's founding family stole the water rights that built three towns. The expedition's benefactor, matriarch Ada Corliss, will kill to keep it buried, and her hired guns are already closing in. Silas, whose own father died as one of Corliss's dispossessed ranchers, must choose between delivering the survivors home quietly and delivering justice loudly. He chooses both — smuggling the people out while mailing copies of the ledger to every courthouse and newspaper in the territory, ending with the Corliss empire collapsing just as Silas finally lets the found family of survivors claim him back.
about_author: Sable Ishikawa is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade running commercial trips through canyon country before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about landscapes that keep secrets and the strangers who become family while carrying them.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Silas Vasquez's POV. A routine patrol across the high desert establishes his solitary life measured in mileage logs and radio silence. He finds fresh tracks where no one should be — a woman on foot, moving fast toward the river. Emotional beat: loneliness so worn it feels like peace, cracked by curiosity.

chapters.title: The Radio Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Dispatch orders him to investigate the Hollis expedition's missed check-ins: eleven scientists and guides, two weeks silent. His supervisor mentions, too casually, that Ada Corliss funded the trip. Emotional beat: duty as habit, unease as something new.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He follows the river upstream, finding the expedition's abandoned supply cache — ransacked from inside, not out. Someone left deliberately and in a hurry. First sign of pursuit: boot prints not matching any expedition member. Emotional beat: dread arriving ahead of understanding.

chapters.title: The Woman on the Trail
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Mara Hollis, the expedition leader's daughter, recalls fleeing camp after her father's death was ruled an accident she didn't believe. Present day, she doubles back and finds Silas tracking her. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into vigilance.

chapters.title: Terms at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Mara holds Silas at arrow-point; he talks her down by knowing things about the terrain she needs. She reveals fragments: her father found something in a cave, and three days later he was dead. Emotional beat: wary negotiation becoming reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Camp of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They reach the original campsite: burned records, a shallow grave marked with river stones, and signs six survivors moved north. Mara identifies the grave digger's boot size as belonging to guide Tomás Reyes — her father's oldest friend. Emotional beat: betrayal suspicion poisoning mourning.

chapters.title: The Corliss Men
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: Corliss foreman Duke Sallow reports to Ada Corliss by shortwave that the ranger has gone upriver. Ada orders the problem handled quietly. We learn she's dying and protecting an inheritance for her grandson. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic dressed as love.

chapters.title: Six Survivors
chapters.summary: Silas and Mara find the survivors holed up in a box canyon: Tomás Reyes, botanist Ines Okafor, grad student Peter Liu, wrangler Cass Duval, medic Ruth Ann, and injured boatman Ferro. Tomás admits moving the body — but says he didn't kill Hollis. Emotional beat: siege mentality, trust rationed like water.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV flashback woven with present. He shows Silas what Hollis found: a leather ledger in the cave, 1890s water rights transfers signed under duress — proof the Corliss fortune began with stolen rivers. Emotional beat: history landing like a physical blow.

chapters.title: Why We Ran
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She recounts the night Hollis died: he announced he'd take the ledger public, and by dawn he was dead and the camp radio smashed. The survivors scattered because they each had reasons to fear being blamed. Emotional beat: guilt as shared inheritance.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Sallow's men hit the canyon at dusk. A firefight leaves one gunman dead and Ferro re-injured. Silas realizes this isn't search-and-rescue anymore — Corliss wants witnesses erased. Emotional beat: the protector's burden settling on his shoulders.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, interior chapter. Around the fire he tells Mara why he measures life in miles: his father lost their ranch to a Corliss water grab and drank himself into the river. Silas took the ranger job to stay moving. Emotional beat: the past surfacing like a drowned thing.

chapters.title: The Split
chapters.summary: Group debate POV rotation. Tomás wants to sell the ledger to a rival family for protection; Ines wants newspapers; Mara wants her father's name cleared first. Silas proposes the impossible: get everyone out alive AND go public. Cass calls it a fantasy. Emotional beat: found family forming through argument.

chapters.title: Sallow's Offer
chapters.summary: Duke Sallow approaches under a white rag: surrender the ledger and the girl, walk away rich. Silas counters by showing him the dead gunman's paybook — Corliss pays in cash, no names, deniable deaths. Sallow leaves thinking. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Narrows
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The group runs the river narrows at night to evade trackers; Ferro's wound opens; Ruth Ann works by headlamp while Cass steers. They lose the supplies raft but gain a day. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into competence — the team becoming a crew.

chapters.title: Peter's Secret
chapters.summary: Peter Liu's POV. He confesses he photographed every ledger page before the camp burned — but mailed the film to his advisor, who may already have told Corliss. That's how the gunmen found them so fast. Emotional beat: shame met, unexpectedly, with forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Town That Water Built
chapters.summary: Silas and Mara slip into Corlissville for supplies and see the empire's face: company store, company church, workers paid in scrip. An old shopkeeper recognizes Silas's surname — knew his father. Emotional beat: inheritance as wound, and as map.

chapters.title: The Shopkeeper's Testimony
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The shopkeeper, Elena Brandt, witnessed the original water seizures as a child and agrees to sign an affidavit if the ledger goes to a federal judge, not local courts Corliss owns. She gives them a name: Judge Amos Pell, two hundred miles east. Emotional beat: courage passed hand to hand across generations.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Crossing
chapters.summary: Action chapter, Silas's POV. Sallow's men ambush them at the ferry crossing. Cass takes a bullet shielding Peter; they escape downstream but Cass is critical. Silas realizes Sallow is herding them, not chasing. Emotional beat: fury sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: Sallow's Doubt
chapters.summary: Sallow's POV. Alone, he reads the ledger pages taken off a dead gunman and finds his own grandfather's X-mark on a coerced transfer. His loyalty cracks. He radios Ada false coordinates. Emotional beat: a mercenary discovering he was always on the wrong side of his own story.

chapters.title: Fever Hours
chapters.summary: Ruth Ann's POV. A quiet chapter fighting Cass's infection with riverbank willow and boiled instruments. Mara and Silas keep watch together and almost speak the thing growing between them. Emotional beat: tenderness as defiance against death.

chapters.title: Ada Corliss
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Dying, she reviews her life: her father's thefts, her marriage of convenience, the grandson she's building a clean legacy for. She orders the survivors' families threatened instead of the survivors — leverage over violence. Emotional beat: love curdled into control.

chapters.title: The Leverage Play
chapters.summary: Group POV rotation. Corliss men detain Tomás's daughter and Ines's brother in town. The group fractures: surrender the ledger or watch families suffer? Silas refuses both options and proposes a third. Emotional beat: despair forced into invention.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Silas's plan revealed: split into two parties. One drives openly toward the judge as bait; the other carries the ledger cross-country on foot. Mara insists on leading the bait run; Silas leads the ledger party. Emotional beat: sacrifice volunteered, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Bait Run
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her truck convoy draws Sallow's main force through the canyonlands in a desperate chase. She uses terrain knowledge Silas taught her to buy hours. Emotional beat: student surpassing teacher, fear outrun by purpose.

chapters.title: Cross-Country
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The ledger party crosses forty miles of dead ground — no water, no shade, Cass carried on a litter. Tomás and Silas finally reconcile over the grave Tomás dug: he was hiding evidence of murder, not committing it. Emotional beat: forgiveness as hard labor.

chapters.title: What Tomás Saw
chapters.summary: Tomás's full testimony. He saw the killer: not a gunman, but expedition sponsor's agent Ward Pellis — and worse, Hollis's own brother-in-law, who'd sold out to Corliss years ago. The truth is uglier than anyone guessed. Emotional beat: the last illusion about the dead man's world breaking.

chapters.title: Radio Silence Broken
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her grandson, Daniel Corliss, intercepts the operation orders and confronts her: he doesn't want an inheritance built on this. She threatens to disown him; he walks out and anonymously tips the territorial newspaper. Emotional beat: the heir refusing the throne.

chapters.title: The Trap Closes
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Sallow, fed false information by his own conscience, misdirects his men — but Ada bypassed him with outside guns. The ledger party is caught in a box canyon at dawn, outnumbered four to one. Emotional beat: the moment before everything breaks.

chapters.title: Standoff at Redrock
chapters.summary: Climax part one, multiple POVs. The standoff turns when Daniel Corliss arrives unarmed and publicly reads the ledger's first page aloud to the hired guns — many of them Corliss-town sons of dispossessed families. Guns waver. Emotional beat: words as weapons stronger than lead.

chapters.title: Sallow's Choice
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Sallow's POV. Ordered to open fire, Sallow instead arrests his own employer's agents, citing the ranger's authority he's spent weeks mocking. A gunfight erupts anyway; Sallow takes a mortal wound shielding Silas. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at full price.

chapters.title: The River Takes Its Due
chapters.summary: Climax part three, Silas's POV. Ward Pellis tries to destroy the ledger in the river; Silas and Mara stop him in the shallows where Hollis died. Pellis confesses to the murder with a dozen witnesses listening. Emotional beat: justice arriving muddy, imperfect, and real.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Miles East
chapters.summary: Transition chapter, Mara's POV. The convoy reaches Judge Pell's courthouse with the ledger, affidavits from Elena Brandt, Peter's photographs, and Pellis's confession. The judge issues warrants before sundown. Emotional beat: exhaustion transformed into vindication.

chapters.title: The Empire Unravels
chapters.summary: Newspaper montage chapter, rotating brief POVs. Headlines cascade: water rights voided, scrip outlawed, Ada Corliss indicted from her deathbed. Ranchers file claims on land their grandparents lost. Emotional beat: history correcting itself in public.

chapters.title: Ada's Last Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's final POV. Dying, she reads the newspaper coverage and writes a letter to Daniel — a full confession meant to spare him the lawsuits, delivered posthumously. She asks the nurse whether stolen water still quenches thirst. Emotional beat: a villain's honest accounting.

chapters.title: Burials
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They bury Sallow beside the river he helped poison and help unpoison. Tomás formally clears Hollis's name at a small service; Mara scatters her father's ashes in the cave where the ledger slept. Emotional beat: grief given ceremony at last.

chapters.title: The Question of Going Home
chapters.summary: Group chapter. Each survivor chooses a path: Ines to publish, Peter to testify, Cass to ranch reclaimed land, Tomás to guide again. All ask Silas to come with them — or rather, ask him to stop leaving. Emotional beat: belonging offered plainly, terrifyingly.

chapters.title: Zero Miles
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He resigns his commission, rides to the rebuilt Brandt store, and finds the whole group waiting with a deed: acreage along the free-running river, all ten names on it. He almost rides past. He doesn't. Emotional beat: the tracker finally letting himself be found.

chapters.title: The Uncharted Trail
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Mara's POV, one year later. The valley has water law, a school, and a trailhead named for Hollis. Silas teaches Mara's survey class to read country the way he does. The last line: some trails aren't charted because they're meant to be walked together. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.
